_comment: Every word the app shows, in one place. Edited here, compiled in - see cmake/UiStrings.cmake; CMake re-runs by itself when this file changes, and nothing extra ships next to the exe. Keys are dotted paths grouped by where the text appears, and become PascalCase identifiers with a k prefix (appearance.showItemBorders -> kAppearanceShowItemBorders). None of this text is an identifier the program depends on: every widget carries its own ##id, so any of it can be reworded freely. A key starting with an underscore is a note like this one and produces nothing.
_tools: The six tools: the name shown in the Shortcuts list, and the tooltips on the selection bar's drawing buttons.
tool.drawTip: Draw - drag on a snippet; hold Shift for a line, Ctrl for a rectangle
tool.eraseTip: Erase - drag over a snippet; hold Ctrl to erase a rectangle
tool.textTip: Text - click the snippet to type into it
tool.selectTip: Select - click a snippet to select it, drag to move it, resize it by dragging just outside its edges (or right-drag it); double-click or hold on it to draw on it; Delete removes it
tool.newScreenshotTip: Screenshot - click for the whole screen or drag an area; then the tool you had is back
tool.newDrawingTip: New drawing - click for the whole screen or drag an area, then draw in it
_create: Actions that happen at once rather than being a tool.
_clipboard: What the clipboard does with the selected snippets - the four rows in the Shortcuts list, on Ctrl+C/X/V and Ctrl+D by default.
_popover: The popover a snippet's More button opens.
popover.backgroundFillTip: Opacity of the background fill color
popover.textSizeTip: Text size, in screen pixels - it doesn't scale when the item is resized
popover.keepAspectTip: Resizing by an edge keeps this snippet's shape - hold Shift for the other way
_menu: The context menus a right-click opens - on a snippet, on a canvas tile in the bar, and on empty canvas. Worded shorter than the popover's tooltips above: a menu row is read at a glance, next to its own icon and its own shortcut, not hovered for an explanation.
_deleted: What the Overview's Show deleted adds: deleted folders and canvases marked out in red, folders holding deleted canvases in yellow, each with Restore and Delete permanently.
deleted.restoreFolderTip: Restore the folder and every deleted canvas in it
deleted.restoreCanvasAndFolderTip: Restore the canvas, and its folder to hold it - the folder's other canvases stay deleted
deleted.deleteDeletedInFolderTip: Delete the deleted canvases in this folder permanently
deleted.goesOnUnknownDate: Deleted permanently on an unknown date
_itemChrome: The buttons on the bar that floats over the selected snippets.
item.pin: Pin - keep it on screen when the overlay is hidden
_toasts: The brief messages that appear after something happened.
toast.copiedWithoutPicture: Copied without its picture - the original's could not be read
toast.purgedOne: 1 folder or canvas deleted over %d days ago was deleted permanently
toast.purgedMany: %zu folders and canvases deleted over %d days ago were deleted permanently
toast.notWritten: Not done - the library could not be written
toast.sentToDeletedCanvasPrefix: Undid paste - back on its deleted canvas, found under Show deleted:
_undoNames: What an undone or redone change is called, after the Undid/Redid prefix above.
_hotkeyText: How a key combination is written out wherever one is shown.
_hud: The edit-mode options' names, in Settings > Behavior and on the Behavior panel.
_behaviorPanel: The Behavior panel, on its own hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+B by default): a window in a corner with the edit-mode options of Settings > Behavior, a number key each. Its rows are the Settings rows' own words. %s in close is the hotkey, in profile the profile's name.
behaviorPanel.title: Behavior
behaviorPanel.defaults: No profile is active, editing behavior defaults
behaviorPanel.footer: Press a row's number to toggle a setting. You can drag the window by its background to move it. To learn more about these options, see {ui:Settings > Behavior}.
_tutorial: The tutorial's cards - see docs/TUTORIAL.md, section 4: each step's title and text, the lines under a text when a step needs something first (need.*) or sees a mistake coming (a step's miss*); the card's own words (card.*), and the card a skip ends on (skipped.*), the list of topics (list.* and topics.*), and its row in Settings > Interaction (settings.*). Step %d of %d takes the step and the count. Wrapped by the card, so written as running text. In braces, filled in as bound and set: {key:<command>} is the key that runs the command of that name (undo, cheatSheet, toggleEditMode, newScreenshotTool), {trigger:screenshot} and {trigger:drawing} the key held for a drag that makes one, {canvas} a canvas's name.
tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to Spickzettel
tutorial.welcome.text:
Spickzettel keeps snippets - screenshots, drawings and notes - over whatever program is underneath, and everything saves itself.

A few steps show you the basics. They run in a folder of their own, so nothing you already have is touched.
tutorial.screenshot.title: Take a screenshot
tutorial.screenshot.text: Drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textTrigger: Hold {trigger:screenshot} and drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textTool: Press {key:newScreenshotTool}, then drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textMenu: Right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:New screenshot}, then drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.missFullscreen: That took the whole screen - a double-click does that. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and drag a box instead.
tutorial.screenshot.missDrawing: That made a drawing rather than a screenshot. Drag a box as above instead.
tutorial.move.title: Move it
tutorial.move.text: Drag it to move it. A press selects it, and a drag takes it along.
tutorial.move.missResized: That changed its size. Drag from the middle to move it.
tutorial.resize.title: Resize it
tutorial.resize.text: Drag just outside a corner or an edge to resize it - the pointer turns into arrows there. A right-drag on the snippet works too, without having to aim exactly. {ui:Shift} toggles the aspect ratio lock.
tutorial.drawingMode.title: Drawing on snippets
tutorial.drawingMode.text: Any snippet can be drawn on, a screenshot as well as a drawing. Double-click it, or hold the button down on it, to draw on it. The pen on its bar does the same once it is selected.
tutorial.draw.title: Draw
tutorial.color.title: Pick a color
tutorial.color.text: Press the color on the bar, and pick another. Click anywhere to close the chooser, then draw with it.
tutorial.color.missNothingDrawn: Give it a try and draw something.
tutorial.width.title: Change the width
tutorial.width.text: While you draw on a snippet, the wheel sets the pen's width. Turn it a few notches, then draw.
tutorial.width.missNothingDrawn: Give it a try and draw something.
tutorial.width.missOpacity: That changed its opacity. Turn the wheel without a key held.
tutorial.line.title: Draw a line
tutorial.line.text: Right-click the pen on the bar, or hold the button down on it, and choose {ui:Line}: its icon turns into a line, and a drag draws a straight one. Holding {ui:Shift} does the same for one stroke.
tutorial.line.missFreehand: That was the pen. Right-click it on the bar and choose {ui:Line}.
tutorial.rectangle.title: Draw a rectangle
tutorial.rectangle.text: The same menu has {ui:Rectangle}: choose it, and drag one. Holding {ui:Ctrl} does the same for one stroke. {ui:Pen}, in the menu, brings the pen back.
tutorial.rectangle.missLine: That was a line. Right-click the pen on the bar and choose {ui:Rectangle}.
tutorial.erase.title: Erase
tutorial.erase.text: Press the eraser on the bar, and drag over what you drew. It cuts through strokes.
tutorial.eraseRect.title: Erase an area
tutorial.eraseRect.text: Right-click the eraser, or hold the button down on it, and choose {ui:Rectangle eraser}. Drag one across what's left. Holding {ui:Ctrl} does the same for one drag.
tutorial.eraseRect.missRound: That was the round eraser. Right-click it on the bar and choose {ui:Rectangle eraser}.
tutorial.eraseRight.title: Erase with the right button
tutorial.eraseRight.text: The right button erases with any tool. Press the pen, then hold the right button and drag across what's left.
tutorial.eraseRight.missEraser: That was the eraser. Press the pen, then drag with the right button.
tutorial.note.title: Write a note
tutorial.note.text: Press {ui:Text} on the bar, click the snippet, and type a note.
tutorial.note.missTyping: Press {ui:Esc} or click outside it when you're done.
tutorial.stopDrawing.title: Stop drawing
tutorial.stopDrawing.text: Click outside it, or press {ui:Esc}, to stop drawing. The tool lit on the bar, pressed again, does it too.
tutorial.delete.title: Delete it
tutorial.delete.text: Select it and press {ui:Delete}, or the close button on its bar.
tutorial.undo.title: Bring it back
tutorial.undo.text: Deleted by mistake? {key:undo} brings it back. It takes back anything you did, a step at a time.
tutorial.undo.textNoKey: Deleted by mistake? Undo brings it back, a step at a time, but it has no key yet. Set one in {ui:Settings > Hotkeys} to use it, and go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.programs.title: Set it up for your programs
tutorial.programs.text: Different applications and games behave differently with an overlay on top. Look through {ui:Settings > Behavior}, and make a profile for each program that needs different settings.
tutorial.antiCheat.title: Careful with anti-cheat
tutorial.antiCheat.text: Some games watch for tools that draw over them or read their input. If a game might object, quit Spickzettel before you start it.
tutorial.exclusiveFullscreen.title: Exclusive fullscreen
tutorial.exclusiveFullscreen.text: The overlay may not work correctly with games running in exclusive fullscreen mode. In such cases, check if the game has support for a borderless window mode.
tutorial.away.title: Back to your program
tutorial.away.text: Press {key:toggleEditMode} to hide the overlay and go back to your program. Press it again to come back here.
tutorial.away.textTray: Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to hide the overlay and go back to your program. Click it again to come back here.
tutorial.end.title: That's the basics
tutorial.end.text:
{key:cheatSheet} shows every key and gesture, and a right-click on anything shows what it can do.

Press {ui:More topics} to explore other functions of the program. You can revisit the tutorial anytime in {ui:Settings > Interaction}.
tutorial.end.textNoCheatSheetKey:
Right-click an empty spot for the cheat sheet, with every key and gesture; a right-click on anything shows what it can do.

{ui:More topics} has the others, and this one again. The tutorial is also in {ui:Settings > Interaction}.
tutorial.drawingEnd.title: That's drawing and notes
tutorial.drawingEnd.text: Double-click any snippet, or press the pen on its bar, to draw on it. {ui:Clear drawing}, in its right-click menu, takes every stroke away; use the {ui:More} button on its bar for per-snippet settings.
tutorial.pin.title: Pin it
tutorial.pin.text: A pinned snippet stays on screen when you hide the overlay, so it can sit over your game while you play. Select it, and press {ui:Pin} on the bar above it.
tutorial.pinnedAway.title: Hide the overlay
tutorial.pinnedAway.text:
Press {key:toggleEditMode} to hide the overlay. The pinned snippet stays over your program, and your clicks go through to it.

Press {key:toggleEditMode} again to come back here.
tutorial.pinnedAway.textTray:
Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to hide the overlay. The pinned snippet stays over your program, and your clicks go through to it.

Click the icon again to come back here.
tutorial.pinnedAway.missViewMode: That was view mode, which keeps everything on screen - it comes next. Hide the overlay as above, and only the pinned snippet stays.
tutorial.opacity.title: Make it see-through
tutorial.opacity.text:
Make it see-through, so it hides less of what's underneath: hold {ui:Ctrl} and turn the wheel.

{ui:Shift} and the wheel fade what's drawn on it instead, and the wheel alone resizes it. {ui:More}, on its bar, has the same as sliders.
tutorial.opacity.missResized: That changed its size. Hold {ui:Ctrl} as you turn the wheel.
tutorial.opacity.missNothingDrawn: {ui:Shift} fades what's drawn on it, and nothing is yet. Hold {ui:Ctrl} instead.
tutorial.viewMode.title: View mode
tutorial.viewMode.text:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

Press {key:toggleViewMode} to switch to it, and {key:toggleEditMode} to come back here.
tutorial.viewMode.textTray:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

Press {key:toggleViewMode} to switch to it, and click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to come back here.
tutorial.viewMode.textNoKey:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

It has no key yet. Set one in {ui:Settings > Hotkeys} to use it, and go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.viewMode.missAway: That hid the overlay, and only what's pinned stayed. Press {key:toggleViewMode} for view mode.
tutorial.unpin.title: Unpin it
tutorial.unpin.text: A pinned snippet stays on screen until you unpin it, even after the tutorial. Press {ui:Pin} on its bar again.
tutorial.pinningEnd.title: That's pinning and view mode
tutorial.pinningEnd.text:
Pin what you need while you play, and make it see-through so it doesn't hide the game. View mode keeps the whole canvas in sight.

The bar's {ui:Fullscreen} fills the screen with a snippet, and its {ui:More} button has the opacity, the background color and the text.
tutorial.newDrawing.title: Make a drawing
tutorial.newDrawing.text: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textTrigger: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Hold {trigger:drawing} and drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textTool: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Press {key:newDrawingTool}, then drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textMenu: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:New drawing}, then drag a box to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.missFullscreen: That took the whole screen - a double-click does that. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and drag a box instead.
tutorial.newDrawing.missScreenshot: That made a screenshot rather than a drawing. Make one as above.
tutorial.fullscreen.title: Screenshot the whole screen
tutorial.fullscreen.text: Double-click an empty spot, or hold the button down on it, to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textTrigger: Hold {trigger:screenshot} and double-click an empty spot, or hold the button down on it, to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textTool: Press {key:newScreenshotTool}, then click anywhere to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textMenu: Right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Fullscreen screenshot} to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDrawingMode: That made a drawing of the whole screen. Press {ui:Esc} to stop drawing on it.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDelete: That made a drawing of the whole screen. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and take a screenshot as above.
tutorial.fullscreen.missBox: That took a part of the screen. Double-click instead of dragging.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDrawing: That made a drawing rather than a screenshot. Take one as above.
tutorial.quickCapture.title: Capture from your program
tutorial.quickCapture.text:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is hidden, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Press {key:toggleEditMode} to hide the overlay, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.

Or press {key:silentCapture} instead: it captures the same way, but the overlay stays hidden, so your game keeps the focus. The capture is there the next time you bring the overlay up.
tutorial.quickCapture.textNoSilent:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is hidden, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Press {key:toggleEditMode} to hide the overlay, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.
tutorial.quickCapture.textTray:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is hidden, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to hide the overlay, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.

Or press {key:silentCapture} instead: it captures the same way, but the overlay stays hidden, so your game keeps the focus. The capture is there the next time you bring the overlay up.
tutorial.quickCapture.textTrayNoSilent:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is hidden, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to hide the overlay, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.
tutorial.quickCapture.textNoKey:
The quick capture takes a screenshot of the whole screen from any program, and brings the overlay up with it, on a new canvas of its own.

It has no working key yet. Set one in {ui:Settings > Hotkeys} to use it, and go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.capturingEnd.title: That's capturing
tutorial.newCanvas.title: A new canvas
tutorial.newCanvas.text: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Move the pointer to the bottom edge of the screen: the canvas bar comes out with this folder's canvases. Press {ui:+} on it for a new canvas.
tutorial.newCanvas.textKey: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Press {key:newCanvas} for a new canvas.
tutorial.newCanvas.textOverview: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Right-click an empty spot, choose {ui:Overview}, and press {ui:New canvas} at the bottom.
tutorial.moveSnippet.title: Take a snippet along
tutorial.moveSnippet.text: To take a snippet to another canvas, select it and press {key:cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold {ui:Alt} and turn the wheel, or click its tile on the canvas bar - and press {key:paste} there.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textNoBar: To take a snippet to another canvas, select it and press {key:cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold {ui:Alt} and turn the wheel - and press {key:paste} there.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textMenu: To take a snippet to another canvas, right-click it and choose {ui:Cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold {ui:Alt} and turn the wheel, or click its tile on the canvas bar - then right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Paste}.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textMenuNoBar: To take a snippet to another canvas, right-click it and choose {ui:Cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold {ui:Alt} and turn the wheel - then right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Paste}.
tutorial.moveSnippet.missCopy: That pasted a copy - the first one is still on the other canvas. Cut it to move it instead.
tutorial.overview.title: The Overview
tutorial.overview.text: The Overview has all your folders and canvases. Open it with the grid button at the right end of the canvas bar.
tutorial.overview.textMenu: The Overview has all your folders and canvases. Right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Overview} to open it.
tutorial.newFolder.title: A new folder
tutorial.newFolder.text: Folders keep canvases apart - one for each game, say. Press {ui:New folder}, at the bottom left. It comes with a canvas, and takes you there.
tutorial.newFolder.missCanvas: That made a canvas. {ui:New folder} is the button to its left.
tutorial.rename.title: A name
tutorial.rename.text: It's named for the time it was made. Double-click the name to change it, and press {ui:Enter}. A canvas is renamed the same way, by the name under its tile.
tutorial.switchFolder.title: Back to the tutorial
tutorial.switchFolder.text: A folder's row shows its canvases. Click the tutorial's folder in the list to see its canvases again.
tutorial.moveCanvas.title: Sort a canvas
tutorial.moveCanvas.text: To move a canvas to another folder, drag its tile onto the folder in the list. Drag one of these onto your folder.
tutorial.deleteCanvas.title: Delete a canvas
tutorial.deleteCanvas.text: The trash button under a tile deletes that canvas, with its snippets. Delete the one your snippet is on.
tutorial.showDeleted.title: The trash
tutorial.showDeleted.text: Nothing deleted is gone yet. Tick {ui:Show deleted}, at the top right: what's in the trash shows in red, where it was.
tutorial.restore.title: Restore
tutorial.restore.text: Press {ui:Restore}, the arrow under its tile: the canvas comes back, with its snippet.
tutorial.openCanvas.title: Open a canvas
tutorial.openCanvas.text: A tile takes you to its canvas and closes the Overview. Click a canvas of the tutorial's to go there.
tutorial.foldersEnd.title: That's folders and canvases
tutorial.foldersEnd.text: A snippet's right-click menu has two more ways to move it: {ui:Move to canvas}, which picks one in the Overview, and {ui:Move to new canvas}. A right-click on a tile of the canvas bar deletes that canvas.
tutorial.capturingEnd.text: Each capture done using the hotkeys is on a canvas of its own, so they're easy to tell apart: the Overview, in the right-click menu, shows them side by side. A right-click on an empty spot also lists every way to make a snippet, with the shortcut keys beside them.
tutorial.openProfiles.title: Profiles
tutorial.openProfiles.text: Different applications - and games in particular - behave differently with the overlay on top. A profile lets you define per-application settings. Right-click an empty spot, choose {ui:Settings}, and pick {ui:Profiles} on the left.
tutorial.openProfiles.textOverview: Different applications - and games in particular - behave differently with the overlay on top. A profile lets you define per-application settings. Press {ui:Settings}, at the top of the Overview, and pick {ui:Profiles} on the left.
tutorial.makeProfile.title: A profile for this program
tutorial.makeProfile.text: The overlay is up over {underneath}. Press {ui:Make a profile for this}: it runs whenever the overlay comes up over {underneath}, and is tagged {ui:Active} while it does.
tutorial.makeProfile.missBlank: That made a blank profile, which matches no program until you name one. {ui:Make a profile for this} is the button to its left.
tutorial.makeProfile.missTaken: {running} is already the profile for {underneath}, and the first in the list that matches is the one that runs. Make another anyway, for practice: it won't run, but the steps work the same.
tutorial.behavior.title: What it can change
tutorial.behavior.text: A profile can change what is in the boxes marked {ui:Per profile}: the settings in {ui:Behavior}, and the shortcuts in {ui:Hotkeys}. Pick {ui:Behavior} on the left.
tutorial.change.title: Change a setting
tutorial.change.text: {ui:Profile}, at the top of the box, says whose settings are below: {profile}'s. Untick {ui:Don't steal focus}. Over {program}, the overlay will now take focus, and the rows under it are grayed out since they depend on that setting. Over any other program the defaults apply.
tutorial.revert.title: Back to the default
tutorial.revert.text: To return a setting to the defaults, press the arrow beside it. Ticking the checkbox again makes it an override for {profile}.
tutorial.revert.missTickedBack: That keeps it {profile}'s own - the row is still in the accent color. The arrow beside it hands it back to the defaults.
tutorial.profilesEnd.title: That's profiles
tutorial.profilesEnd.text: {ui:New empty profile} makes one for a program that isn't in front. Open a profile's row to add more programs to it, or part of a window's title. The first profile in the list that matches is the one that runs.
tutorial.need.inTutorialFolder: The tutorial is in a folder of its own.
tutorial.need.closeOverview: Close the Overview to go on.
tutorial.need.closeCheatSheet: Close the cheat sheet to go on.
tutorial.need.closePopup: Press {ui:Esc} to close what is open, and go on.
tutorial.need.noDrawingMode: Click outside the snippet, or press {ui:Esc}, to stop drawing first.
tutorial.need.noOtherTool: Press {ui:Esc} to put the tool down first.
tutorial.need.aSubject: Take a screenshot to practice on, or let me put one here.
tutorial.need.subjectOnScreen: It went to the dock. Click it there to bring it back.
tutorial.need.subjectCanMove: It fills the screen. Right-click it and choose {ui:Fullscreen} to shrink it back.
tutorial.need.drawingOnSubject: Double-click it to draw on it again.
tutorial.need.deletedSubject: Delete it again to try this, or go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.need.subjectPinned: It isn't pinned. Select it, and press {ui:Pin} on its bar.
tutorial.need.penInHand: Press the pen on the bar.
tutorial.need.subjectDrawnOn: Nothing is drawn on it to erase. Draw something with the pen first.
tutorial.need.overviewUp: Open the Overview: right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Overview}.
tutorial.need.canvasesTab: Go back to the {ui:Canvases} tab, at the top left.
tutorial.need.deletedShown: Tick {ui:Show deleted}, at the top right, to see it.
tutorial.need.somethingInTrash: Nothing of the tutorial's is in the trash. Delete a canvas first, or go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.need.settingsUp: Open Settings: right-click an empty spot and choose {ui:Settings}.
tutorial.need.settingsTab: Press {ui:Settings}, at the top of the Overview.
tutorial.need.profilesSection: Pick {ui:Profiles} in the list on the left.
tutorial.need.behaviorSection: Pick {ui:Behavior} in the list on the left.
tutorial.need.aProgramUnderneath: The overlay is up over nothing it can name. Press {key:toggleEditMode} to hide it, click the program you want a profile for, and press it again.
tutorial.need.aProgramUnderneathTray: The overlay is up over nothing it can name. Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to hide it, click the program you want a profile for, and click the icon again.
tutorial.need.tutorialsProfile: The tutorial has no profile of its own: it was deleted, or the app has restarted since. Go {ui:Back} to make one, or go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.need.showingIt: {ui:Profile} is on {showing}. Pick {profile} there: a change is made to whose settings it shows.
tutorial.need.somethingSetInIt: {profile} sets nothing of its own yet. Untick {ui:Don't steal focus} in it first, or go on with {ui:Next}.
tutorial.card.nextWaits: The next steps use what this one makes.
tutorial.skipped.title: Tutorial skipped
tutorial.skipped.again: {ui:More topics} has this one again, and the others. The tutorial is also in {ui:Settings > Interaction}.
tutorial.list.title: Tutorial
tutorial.list.text: Pick a topic. Most tutorials run in a new folder of their own.
tutorial.settings.heading: Tutorial
tutorial.settings.help:
The tutorial tells you about different functions of the app. Take any topic again whenever you want a refresher.

Most topics run in a new folder of their own, away from your canvases.
tutorial.topics.basics.title: Basics
tutorial.topics.basics.gist: Take a screenshot, move and resize it, delete it and bring it back, and go back to your program.
tutorial.topics.pinning.title: Pinning and view mode
tutorial.topics.pinning.gist: Keep a snippet on screen over your program, make it see-through, and let your clicks through.
tutorial.topics.drawing.title: Drawing and notes
tutorial.topics.drawing.gist: Draw on a snippet: the color, the width, shapes, the eraser, and a note.
tutorial.topics.capturing.title: Capturing
tutorial.topics.capturing.gist: Make a drawing, screenshot the whole screen, and capture from your program with a hotkey.
tutorial.topics.folders.title: Folders and canvases
tutorial.topics.folders.gist: Make and switch canvases, move a snippet, sort canvases into folders, and restore from the trash.
tutorial.topics.profiles.title: Profiles
tutorial.topics.profiles.gist: Make a profile for a program, change a setting in it, and hand it back to the defaults.
_cheatSheet: The cheat sheet (Ctrl+H by default): every key and gesture, in groups. Each row is what you press, then what it does; a shortcut that is unbound drops its row. After a modifier, a gesture is capitalized like a key (Ctrl+Drag), so the left column reads as one kind of thing.
cheatSheet.title: Cheat sheet
cheatSheet.quickCapture: Capture the screen to a new canvas

_status: The warning along the bottom while the disk cannot be written to - see OverlayApp::RenderPersistenceWarning. %s is a path.
status.writeFailed: Could not write to the library at %s, so the last change was not made - it is back as it was
status.configWriteFailed: Could not write the settings to %s
_startup: The message boxes shown when the app cannot start at all, before there is a tray icon to say so.
startup.failed: Spickzettel could not start. Another copy may already be running.
startup.configSetAside:
Spickzettel could not read its settings file, %s, and started with the default settings.

The file was kept beside it as %s, so nothing in it is lost. Deleting deleted folders and canvases permanently is switched off until it is switched on again in Settings > Behavior.
startup.configUnreadable:
Spickzettel could not read its settings file, %s, and started with the default settings.

The file was left as it is, and settings changed until the next start will not be saved. Nothing deleted was erased for good at this start.
startup.configNewer: Spickzettel's settings file, %s, was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel. This version started with what it could read from it and leaves the file as it is, so settings changed until the next start will not be saved. Nothing deleted was erased for good at this start.
startup.librarySetAside:
Spickzettel could not read its library file, %s - it is not a library this version can open, or it is damaged - and started with an empty library.

The file was kept beside it as %s, so nothing in it is lost.
startup.hotkeysTaken:
Spickzettel started, but these hotkeys are already used by another application and do nothing:
%s

The tray icon's menu opens the overlay without them, and Settings > Hotkeys can give them other keys.
startup.newerLibrary: Spickzettel could not start: your library was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel. This version would lose what the newer one saved, so it leaves the library alone. Please use the newer version.
startup.runningWithDataDir: Spickzettel could not start with its own data folder: another copy is running. Quit that copy first.
startup.commandLine:
Spickzettel could not start: %s

It takes these options:%s
_commandLine: The command-line options, for the scripts that test and measure the app: the help of each, and what is said about arguments that are wrong. %s is the argument or the option's name.
commandLine.dataDir: Keeps the settings, the library and the crash dumps in this folder instead of your own.
commandLine.unknown: %s is not an option it knows.
startup.libraryUnreadable: Spickzettel could not start: it could not read its library file, %s. Nothing was changed. Another program may be holding it - a backup or sync tool, say - or the file's permissions may not let Spickzettel read it. Start Spickzettel again once the file can be read.
_tray: The system tray icon's own menu.
_placeholders: Some strings below carry printf placeholders - %s for a word, %zu for a count, %d%% for a percentage. Keep every one of them, and in the same order: they are filled in at runtime, and a missing or extra one is a crash rather than a typo.
_formats: How a number reads where one is shown - the unit, and the spacing before it.
_overview: The panel the canvas bar's Overview button opens: three tabs across the top, and the canvas grid under the first.
overview.showDeletedHelp: Show deleted folders and canvases, to restore or delete permanently
overview.emptyTrashHelp: Delete every deleted folder and canvas permanently
overview.previewsVectorHelp: Show strokes in canvas previews. Turn off if the Overview feels slow.
overview.previewsBitmapHelp: Show screenshots in canvas previews. Turn off if the Overview feels slow.
overview.folderEmpty: This folder has no canvases yet.
overview.libraryEmpty: No canvases anywhere yet - "New canvas" makes one.
_moveCopy: The picker an item's "Move to another canvas" opens, and the button that confirms it.
_deleteConfirm: The confirmation before a canvas or folder is deleted, and before anything already deleted is deleted for good.
deleteConfirm.promptDeletedIn: Delete the deleted canvases in "%s" permanently?
deleteConfirm.trashContentsOne: The one deleted folder or canvas is deleted permanently, with everything in it.
deleteConfirm.trashContentsMany: The %zu deleted folders and canvases are deleted permanently, with everything in them.
deleteConfirm.alsoCanvases: This also deletes every canvas inside it.
deleteConfirm.alsoCanvasesMany: This also deletes every canvas inside them.
deleteConfirm.restorable: It can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview.
deleteConfirm.restorableFor: It can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview for %d days. After that it is deleted permanently.
deleteConfirm.restorableMany: They can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview.
deleteConfirm.restorableForMany: They can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview for %d days. After that they are deleted permanently.
_libraryReminder: The box shown when the library has grown past the size set in Settings > Behavior, once per start. %s in text is the size, as "2.3 GB".
libraryReminder.hint: Deleted folders and canvases stay in the trash until it is emptied: turn on "Show deleted" in the Overview and press "Empty trash". In Settings > Behavior they can be deleted from the trash automatically after a number of days, and this reminder can be changed or turned off.
_settingsTabs: The list down the left of the Settings tab.
settings.scopeProfileNote: Settings that can be overridden per profile
settings.notSavedNewer: Changes made here apply until Spickzettel exits, and are not saved: the settings file, %s, was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel and is left as it is.
settings.notSavedUnreadable: Changes made here apply until Spickzettel exits, and are not saved: the settings file, %s, could not be read and is left as it is.
_defaults: Settings > Defaults: what a new snippet starts with.
defaults.screenshotHelp:
What a screenshot starts with when it is made.

Each of these is the snippet's own from then on, changed in its popover (the More button on its bar). Changing one here leaves every snippet already made as it is.
defaults.drawingHelp:
What a drawing starts with when it is made.

A drawing starts see-through. Raise its background opacity to give every new one a backing, in the color below.

Each of these is the snippet's own from then on, changed in its popover (the More button on its bar). Changing one here leaves every snippet already made as it is.
defaults.textHelp:
The size and color text starts with in a new snippet.

The size is in screen pixels, and does not change when the snippet is resized. It starts at 20, times the display scale Windows had when Spickzettel first ran.

The color's alpha is the text's opacity.
defaults.keepAspectHelp:
Resizing by an edge keeps the snippet's shape. Hold Shift while dragging for the other way.

A snippet's own popover can change this for that snippet alone.
appearance.monitorHelp:
Which monitor the overlay comes up on.

{ui:Primary display} is whichever monitor Windows treats as the main one. Pick a monitor by name and the overlay stays with that monitor. While it isn't connected the overlay uses the primary display, and it goes back as soon as the monitor returns.

A change applies at once, with the overlay moving to the monitor you picked.
appearance.uiScaleHelp:
How large the overlay's own text, buttons and panels are drawn.

{ui:Match Windows} uses the scale Windows is set to for the monitor the overlay is on (Settings > System > Display > Scale), and follows it when that changes. Alternatively, you can pick a custom size independent of the setting in Windows.

Note that snippet contents (drawings, screenshots, text) keep their own sizes, independent of this setting.
appearance.accentHelp:
The default color used for various user interface elements and selections. Text and icons drawn on it switch between dark and light to stay readable.

This color is also used for selected snippets by default, but you can set a custom color for that under Snippet border colors.
appearance.showItemBorders: Show a border around every snippet, not just the frontmost
appearance.showHelpTooltips: Show help when the pointer rests on a button or option
appearance.imageFilterHelp:
How screenshots are drawn when they are shown larger or smaller than they were taken.

Takes effect immediately; the pictures themselves are not changed and can be reset to their original size using the context menu of a snippet.
appearance.imageFilterLanczos: Lanczos (sharpest, may cause faint halos, more memory usage)
appearance.snippetColorsHelp:
Different colors for different states of a snippet, to tell them apart at a glance.

Hovering is shown separately, as a thicker border.
appearance.selectedBorderFollowsAccent: Use the accent color for the selected border
appearance.showEditBorder: Show a border around the screen while edit mode is active
appearance.showEditBorderHelp:
A frame around the whole screen while the overlay is in edit mode, so it's obvious your clicks are landing here rather than in whatever's underneath. Particularly useful while a canvas is still empty.

View-only mode never draws it - input passes straight through there.
appearance.editBorderEmptyOnly: Show border only while the canvas is still empty
appearance.editBorderEmptyOnlyHelp: The border disappears as soon as there's anything on the current canvas, since that already shows the overlay is active.
appearance.showCanvasBar: Show the canvas bar at the bottom of the screen in edit mode
appearance.showCanvasBarHelp: A bar along the bottom edge with the canvases of the folder you are in, to switch between them, start a new one, or delete them. It slides out when the pointer reaches the bottom of the screen, and for a moment whenever the canvas changes or the overlay comes up.
_dock: The dock along the bottom, where minimized snippets wait.
_drawing: Settings > Interaction: the Snippets section at its top.
_bars: Settings > Interaction: the bar that floats over the selection, and the buttons its two groups carry.
bars.heading: Toolbar above a snippet
bars.help: The small bar that floats over a selected snippet. You can customize which buttons are relevant to you and should be shown by enabling or disabling them here. Drag a button onto another to move it there.
bars.resetTip: Put this row back the way it ships: every button, in its original order
drawing.raiseSelected: Bring a snippet to the front when selecting it
drawing.raiseSelectedHelp: Clicking or dragging a snippet automatically moves it to the front. When disabled, you can still reorder snippets by using their context menu.
creation.heading: Making a snippet on an empty spot
creation.help: What a press of the left button on empty space makes. Combine with different modifiers (or none) to make different kinds of snippets. Dragging makes a snippet of the dragged size; double-clicking or holding makes a fullscreen one.
settings.deletedHeading: Folder and canvas deletion and retention
settings.confirmDelete: Ask before moving folders and canvases to the trash
settings.confirmDeleteHelp: Asks before a folder or canvas is deleted (moved to trash) in the canvas bar or the overview. It can still be restored afterwards, with {ui:Show deleted} in the Overview.
settings.confirmDeleteForGood: Ask before deleting folders and canvases permanently
settings.confirmDeleteForGoodHelp: Asks before a folder or canvas that is already in the trash is deleted permanently when you use {ui:Show deleted} in the Overview. That cannot be undone.
settings.purgeDeleted: Delete items in the trash after
settings.librarySizeReminder: Notify me when the library is larger than
settings.librarySizeReminderHelp: Checked when Spickzettel starts. A library over this size shows a reminder the next time the overlay is up, with the ways to make it smaller.
settings.purgeDeletedHelp:
Anything that has been in the trash longer than this is deleted permanently the next time Spickzettel starts.

Off by default: the trash keeps everything until you empty it. Turn on {ui:Show deleted} in the Overview and press {ui:Empty trash}.

Deleted individual snippets are not kept in the trash and don't survive a restart of the app. You can use undo to quickly fix small accidents.
debug.heading: Debugging and monitoring overlays
debug.showDebugOverlayHelp:
Border around the screen plus a status line (stroke count, mouse position) - confirms the overlay is receiving input at all.

In edit mode, also what the {ui:Behavior} options are doing: the frame rate, the pointer's steps while the mouse is read raw, how late the countering lands, and which application is in front and whether it is elevated above us.
debug.showFrameGraphHelp: A graph of the last ten seconds, top right: how long each frame took to come, and under it when the library was written or flushed to the disk, a picture encoded or read, the screen captured or the settings saved - for telling what a stutter was.

_input: Settings > Behavior - what the overlay does to the application underneath.
input.underneathHelp: The application the overlay is currently up over, shown to help you match the profiles below.
input.nothingIdentifiable: Nothing identifiable - no window in front, or one that won't say what it is.
input.unreadableExecutableHelp: Its image path can't be read from here. That means a program belonging to another account, or a game shielded by anti-cheat - not simply one running as administrator, which answers like any other. Match it on its window title instead.
input.editModeHelp:
How the overlay behaves while the respective profile is active. Which combination works depends on the application or game, so they stay separately switchable. Some settings depend on others as indicated by the tree structure.

To try them out in front of the game, the {ui:Behavior panel} hotkey brings them up there, a key each (see {ui:Hotkeys}).
input.dontStealFocusHelp:
Keeps a game from going into its pause screen or muting itself while the overlay is up.

Alternatively, turn this off and look in the game's own settings for how it behaves when it loses focus.

If the game supports it, taking focus from the game properly may help to keep keystrokes and mouse input from reaching it.
input.dontForwardKeystrokesHelp:
Tries to keep keystrokes from reaching the underlying application while it keeps focus.

The hotkeys keep working, including the one that hides the overlay again. Certain Windows shortcuts - the Windows key, Alt+Tab - are also affected by this setting.

A game reading the keyboard directly may still receive keys. In such cases, stealing the focus from the game may help, as long as the game doesn't break when focus is taken away from it.
input.rawMouseHelp:
With this enabled, the mouse pointer is driven by reading input from the hardware directly instead of from the Windows cursor. That is what makes the overlay usable over a game that hides the pointer, pins it, or snaps it back to the middle of the screen. Clicks and drags over the overlay also no longer reach the game.

Oftentimes this does not stop the game looking around. First-person games read mouse movement directly as well, so expect the camera to keep turning while you draw. The {ui:Counter raw mouse input} together with {ui:Freeze screen while editing} settings below may help in that case.
input.takeFocusOverElevatedHelp:
Windows doesn't pass any input to the overlay while an application with higher privileges is in front - for example Task Manager on an account with administrator rights.

To keep the overlay functional, you can choose to take focus from such applications despite the {ui:Don't steal focus} setting.

Note that detection may not be perfect and is done on a best-effort basis.
input.counterRawMouseHelp:
Tries to send opposing mouse input to the game to keep a first-person camera roughly in the same spot when the overlay is hidden again.

Particularly useful together with the {ui:Freeze screen while editing} option below to hide camera movements while the overlay is up.

Note that some games may ignore synthetic input such that the countering has no effect.
input.counterThresholdHelp: How far the pointer may move in either axis before countering takes effect. A lower value may help keep the camera more steady at the expense of a higher frequency of corrections, which may in turn lead to pointer stutters in the overlay.
input.softwarePointerHelp:
Whether the overlay draws its own pointer instead of using the default Windows pointer. In combination with raw mouse input, this offers a usable pointer even if the underlying application or game interferes with the real pointer position (e.g. puts it back to the screen center every frame).

When not using raw mouse input, this is purely cosmetic - Windows is moving the pointer and this only changes how it looks.
input.freezeScreenHelp:
Show a screenshot of the whole screen instead of the live screen while the overlay is up. This hides a first-person camera that keeps moving underneath. Switching this on takes effect the next time the overlay comes up.

A game in exclusive fullscreen may refuse to be captured; if the screen comes up blank rather than frozen, switch that game to borderless windowed mode.

A screenshot snippet taken while the screen is frozen is cut out of the frozen picture instead of the live screen.
_hotkeys: Settings > Hotkeys, and the Shortcuts rows below them.
hotkeys.summoningHelp:
The keys that reach the overlay from anywhere, whatever has focus. Click one and press the combination you want.

These are the same everywhere, including in the profiles below: Windows hands a registered combination to one application system-wide, so a key this claims here is claimed in every application.
hotkeys.sayWhenHidden: Show a message for a background capture while the overlay is hidden
hotkeys.sayWhenHiddenHelp:
A background capture puts a message on screen for a moment, so a hotkey that shows you nothing still tells you it worked.

This is only relevant when the overlay is hidden. With the overlay already up, in either mode, the message is always shown.
hotkeys.comboPrompt: Press a key... (click again to cancel)
hotkeys.comboTooltip: Click, then press the key combo you want - modifiers optional
hotkeys.comboRejected: Couldn't set that hotkey - it is already taken by another app
hotkeys.comboSetHere: Set here. Click to go back to the default (%s)
hotkeys.shortcutsHelp:
Keys that pick a tool, start something new, undo, move snippets through the clipboard, or open the cheat sheet, while the overlay is up in edit mode.

Click a row, then press the key you want, or the middle or a side mouse button; Escape leaves it unbound. A key can only belong to one row, so taking it from another row is what happens if you reuse it.

In a text field, the usual keys apply instead, whatever is set here: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+A.
hotkeys.shortcutPrompt: Press a key or button... (Esc clears)
hotkeys.shortcutTooltip: Click, then press the key or mouse button you want - or Escape to leave it unbound
hotkeys.shortcutSetHere: Set here. Click to go back to the default binding (%s)
_profiles: Settings > Profiles, and the target picker shared with the other tabs. The tag* strings are the boxes after a profile's name; %zu is a count.
profiles.showingSettingsHelp:
Choose a profile for which you would like to change the settings below.

A profile either sets a custom value for each setting below, or it takes the value from the defaults. Overridden settings carry a revert arrow that sets them back to the default.

Editing a profile that isn't the one running is allowed - it just doesn't change anything until the overlay comes up over an application it matches.
profiles.showingShortcutsHelp:
Choose a profile for which to define shortcuts to use within the overlay. You can override some of the keys per profile, the others are taken from the defaults. Overridden keys carry a revert arrow that sets them back to the default.

Editing a profile that isn't the one running is allowed - it just doesn't change anything until the overlay comes up over an application it matches.
profiles.help:
A profile changes the Behavior settings and the Shortcuts while the overlay is up over one particular application. One applies at a time - the first in this list whose rules match - and everything that is not overridden comes from the defaults.

A profile with no applications listed matches nothing and thus never applies.

A change to which applications a profile matches takes effect the next time the overlay is opened.
profiles.nothingToMake: Nothing identifiable to make a profile for.
profiles.makeForThisTooltip: Matched on the executable name, which is the half that doesn't change
profiles.newProfileTooltip: For an application that isn't in front of you - open it and name what it matches
profiles.tagActiveTooltip: The overlay is up over an application this profile matches, so its overrides are in effect
profiles.tagNoCriteria: No matching criteria set up yet
profiles.name: Name
profiles.nameTaken: Another profile is already called "%s". This one keeps its name until you type one that is free.
profiles.nothingToMatchOn: Nothing to match on, so this profile never applies.
